name: The Pike household at 2101 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_pike_eugene_s

present_on_scene_date.note: The household is listed at 2101 Prairie Avenue in both the 1904 and 1905 editions of the Blue Book, which bracket 1 July 1904, but not with the same people: the 1905 list prints 2101 Mr. & Mrs. Eugene S. Pike (the reading of the 1905 page stops there; the younger Pikes were not checked). Each person's own note says which of them the later list drops or adds.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2101, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The seven live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: Rockwell (a mother-in-law of 88 in 1900, the given name unread; no 1904 source puts her here). The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.
